title: Ékezetek
summary: Accent marks make a vowel long, and a long vowel can be a completely different word.

sections.text: Hungarian has **14 vowels**: a short and a long version of each. The mark **´** makes a vowel long; on ö and ü the long version gets a double mark: **ő, ű**.
**a/á** and **e/é** differ in sound, not just length: *a* is like the “o” in British “hot”, *á* like the “a” in “father”. *e* is like “e” in “bed”, *é* like “ay” in “say” (without the y glide).
Tap the speaker to hear each pair. Leaving out an accent can turn a bed into a brain.
